claims.text: Machine-learning algorithms can improve the accuracy of melting-temperature predictions for high-entropy alloys relative to current experimental and computational methods.
Machine-learning algorithms can improve the accuracy of fusion-enthalpy and fusion-entropy predictions for high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning algorithms can improve the accuracy of predictions of volume change upon melting for high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning algorithms can improve the accuracy of liquid-state thermodynamic-property predictions for high-entropy alloys.
Machine learning can determine the listed thermodynamic properties more efficiently across a large compositional space than current experimental and computational methods.
Existing high-entropy-alloy discovery and computational methods face efficiency and capability limitations.
Finite-temperature experimental data for relevant high-entropy alloys are incomplete.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn patterns in thermodynamic data.
Machine-learning predictions can reflect the underlying physics of high-entropy alloys.
Static and dynamic lattice distortions influence structural, mechanical, elastic, and thermodynamic characteristics of high-entropy alloys.
Scaling laws for lattice distortions provide a relevant physical basis for predicting the specified melting and liquid thermodynamic properties.
The proposed approach applies across various high-entropy-alloy compositions in both high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality and quantity of the machine-learning training data.
Application of the proposed machine-learning approach to high-entropy alloys requires further validation.
